text:
alex-customer: Hi team — after yesterday's model upgrade our embeddings ingestion pipeline started rejecting vectors. We expect dim=1536 but the API returned 768 for the same payload. Can someone look?

jess-support: Sorry about that, alex. Can you paste the request you used and a snippet of the error from your indexer?

alex-customer: Error from indexer: "vector length 768 != expected 1536 for index 'kb_v2'".
Here's the curl I used:
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"embed-alpha","input":["what is our refund policy",""]}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```
(most requests are batched arrays of 8-16 docs)

mike-ml: Thanks. Did you have model pinned to a specific variant or using the catalog alias?

alex-customer: We pinned to "embed-alpha:stable" last year. No changes on our side. This started after your upgrade window.

jess-support: @mike-ml can you check routing/fallback rules? This smells like a fallback to a smaller embed model under batch conditions.

mike-ml: Looking at the serving logs for that customer id — I see requests routed to embed-alpha-v3 (1536) usually, but at ~2026-06-12T03:14Z a subset of batched requests were routed to embed-alpha-lite-q (768) when the quantized pool handled the batch. There was a recent canary tweak that allows cross-variant fallback if pinned variant is unavailable.

sam-infra: To be explicit: the pinned alias "embed-alpha:stable" resolved to a group that included both v3 (fp16, 1536) and a legacy quant variant (lite-q, 768). Under heavy batching the runtime preferred a lower-memory quant variant to keep latency SLOs. That caused the dimension flip.

jess-support: Oof. So customer pin semantics didn't prevent fallback to quantized variants?

mike-ml: Correct — bug in alias-resolution logic: pinned alias honored version family but not "embedding dimensionality" constraint. We'll push a hotfix to treat embedding-dim as a matching constraint for alias resolution.

alex-customer: What's the immediate mitigation? We need our indexer to stop failing.

mike-ml: Short-term workarounds: 1) Explicitly request the full variant id (e.g., model: "embed-alpha-v3") in your request; 2) Set header "X-Redwood-Prefer-No-Fallback: true" to disable cross-variant fallback; 3) Reduce batch size to 1-2 to avoid routing into quant pool.

jess-support: I'll apply a temporary policy on your account to pin you to the v3 variant while we deploy the fix. @sam-infra can you enable that for org org-9882?

sam-infra: Done — org-9882 is now forced to embed-alpha-v3 for embeddings. Can you retry, alex?

alex-customer: Retrying now... (runs few samples)
alex-customer: Success — vectors are 1536 again and ingestion is happy. Thanks.

mike-ml: Root cause: alias resolution allowed fallback to quantized family when memory pressure + batching heuristics triggered. Fix landed in routing service: treat embedding vector_size as a hard attribute for alias match and add unit tests.

jess-support: We'll keep the temporary force-pin until tomorrow's deploy finishes. Apologies for the disruption, alex.

alex-customer: Appreciate the quick turnaround. One ask: can you emit a header or response field showing resolved_variant_id in responses? That would help us detect future silent flips.

mike-ml: Good idea — adding X-Redwood-Model-Id header and response.meta.resolved_variant in the next patch. Will follow up with a changelog entry.

deploy-bot: deploy service: routing-service/patch-embed-dim-fix @ 1765432160 — canary 10% -> 100%

sam-infra: Patch promoted. We'll monitor for any regressed fallbacks.

jess-support: Closing this thread after confirmation from alex. Please reopen if you see further issues. :slightly_smiling_face:

alex-customer: All good for now. Thank you! :tada:
